evaluation.positioning_hook: A lonely teenage poet falls hard for the one girl who sees him, then has to survive the kind of loss that turns first love into a lifelong wound.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The emotional lane is clear and evergreen: first love, grief, and memory. The challenge is that the script plays as a very intimate, poetic romance with limited external engine, so the audience is real but narrower than a broad commercial feature.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The central premise lands quickly: Pierre is isolated, Celia enters his life, and the bracelet/poem motif ties the relationship to the loss. The hook is understandable, but the script is more mood-and-montage than a sharply articulated feature engine.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Pierre has a clear emotional wound and Celia has warmth and initiative, which gives the relationship a pulse. They are more archetypal than fully individualized on the page, so the roles function better as a showcase than as especially durable star vehicles.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The poem-forward structure and visualized memory fragments give the script a distinct authorial register. That said, the underlying story is a familiar young-love-to-loss arc, so the boldness lives more in presentation than in premise.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The script moves in emotional beats rather than escalating dramatic turns, with long stretches of lyrical montage and reflective voiceover. The church eulogy and coffin reveal the destination, but the middle section has limited forward pressure.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The bracelet, the poem, and the rain motif create a recognizable emotional signature. The effect is sincere, but the story itself remains close to a familiar tragic-romance template.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The world is essentially a school, a field, a hospital, and a church, used as emotional backdrops rather than a textured social ecosystem. There is little sense of a larger environment generating story beyond the central relationship.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a consistent elegiac, poetic tone, and it commits to that register from the opening voiceover through the funeral. The tone is distinctive in texture, though it can feel repetitive because the same emotional note is sustained almost throughout.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: The grief framing and recurring imagery suggest a deeper interior life for Pierre, especially around memory and self-worth. On the page, though, that depth is implied more than dramatized, so the script hints at more than it fully delivers.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: This is fundamentally a two-character romance with very limited supporting interaction. Pierre and Celia carry the piece, but there is not much ensemble energy or recurring relationship web beyond them.

lead_characters.name: Pierre
lead_characters.demographics: Teenage male, likely 16-17, introverted high-school student, emotionally sensitive, writer/poet.
lead_characters.hook: Pierre is the isolated, self-erasing boy at the center of the piece: awkward in class, defensive when someone gets close, and quietly desperate to be seen. His poetry is his private language, and Celia becomes the first person who treats that inner life as something worth loving; after her loss, he turns grief into ritual, memory, and voiceover.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Timothée Chalamet in Call Me by Your Name — a tender, inward lead whose face has to carry longing, embarrassment, and heartbreak in close-up. It gives an actor the chance to play silence as subtext and then land the emotional release in the funeral speech and final voiceover.

lead_characters.name: Celia
lead_characters.demographics: Teenage female, likely 16-17, warm, socially confident, emotionally perceptive.
lead_characters.hook: Celia is the bright force who notices Pierre before anyone else does, and she does it with ease rather than pity. She is written as the emotional catalyst of the story — playful, encouraging, and romantic — and then becomes the memory the film keeps returning to after her death.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of luminous, scene-stealing part that gave Rachel McAdams in The Notebook or Hailee Steinfeld in The Edge of Seventeen a chance to define the emotional temperature of the movie. The role offers charm, warmth, and the tragic afterimage that makes the audience feel the loss.

casting_characteristics: Teenage lead and teenage female co-star

technical.vfx_details: No visible VFX requirement beyond simple title/transition styling if desired.
technical.sfx_needs: Minimal practical needs: rain effect, coffin/funeral dressing, music playback, and montage styling.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: specialty streaming debut or limited theatrical play for a young-adult romance/drama.

budget.note: Contemporary, small cast, five practical locations, no VFX, no stunts, and minimal effects work — this sits comfortably in a low-cost feature package.

casting.note: The lead needs a teenager or very young-looking actor who can carry interior poetry, awkward comedy, and grief without flattening into one note. Celia also needs immediate warmth and natural charisma to make the relationship feel lived-in.

development.note: The script is built around mood, voiceover, and montage, so the main development conversation is whether the emotional beats can carry feature length without a stronger dramatic engine. The funeral reveal and poem motif give it shape, but the middle section remains light on escalation.

comp_set.title: The Fault in Our Stars
comp_set.why_it_comps: Shares the young-love-through-loss emotional lane and the audience promise of romance that turns into grief.

comp_set.title: A Walk to Remember
comp_set.why_it_comps: Matches the earnest, tearjerker romance structure where a gentle relationship is defined by mortality and memory.

comp_set.title: Call Me by Your Name
comp_set.why_it_comps: Comps on lyrical intimacy, first-love subjectivity, and the way memory becomes the real dramatic engine.

comp_set.title: The Spectacular Now
comp_set.why_it_comps: Shares the teen-romance realism and the focus on an emotionally fragile young lead whose inner life drives the movie.

audience_target.primary_audience: Viewers who respond to earnest young-adult romance and grief-forward love stories, especially audiences that like emotional, music-driven features.
audience_target.demographics: Teens through adults 35+, with a strong skew toward women and young adults who watch relationship-driven streaming dramas.

budget_tier.note: Small cast, contemporary settings, and no VFX keep this in indie-feature territory; music licensing for the Novo Amor tracks is the main variable.

types_of_buyers: specialty streamers looking for emotional date-night titles
indie distributors with a young-adult romance lane
producers seeking low-cost, actor-forward prestige romance
lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally beside intimate, emotionally legible romance features that sell on feeling, soundtrack, and a strong central performance rather than plot machinery.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature; the story resolves as a self-contained romance-and-loss piece with no clear franchise or spinoff vector.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The poem is the movie's signature device.
strengths.what_it_means: That gives the project a clear marketing and emotional hook: a romance defined by a recurring piece of writing, memory, and music. Buyers who want a lyrical, youth-skewing tearjerker can immediately understand the promise.
strengths.evidence: Celia reads Pierre's poem, the poem returns in voiceover, and the final funeral speech circles back to the same language.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The bracelet creates a clean visual motif.
strengths.what_it_means: A simple recurring object helps the film feel cohesive and gives the audience something to remember after the emotional beats. That kind of motif is useful for posters, trailers, and the kind of word-of-mouth that comes from a strong image.
strengths.evidence: The bracelet appears at the start, is gifted in the relationship montage, and returns in the final floating image.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The production footprint is very lean.
strengths.what_it_means: This is the kind of feature that can be mounted without heavy infrastructure, which lowers buyer risk and broadens the pool of indie financiers and streaming buyers. A director can make a strong calling-card film here without needing scale.
strengths.evidence: The script lives in a bedroom, classroom, school grounds, hospital room, and church, with no VFX or stunt load.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Pierre is a strong actor-facing grief role.
strengths.what_it_means: The lead part offers a clear emotional arc from isolation to connection to mourning, which is exactly the kind of material that can elevate a young actor's profile. That makes the project attractive to talent reps looking for a showcase with sensitivity rather than spectacle.
strengths.evidence: Pierre's stammered classroom exchanges, the poem reveal, the hospital bedside scenes, and the funeral speech all lean on performance.

whats_special.headline: This is a low-cost, actor-forward romance with a built-in emotional signature: the poem, the bracelet, and the grief arc give it a clean identity that can travel on streaming and specialty indie lanes. It is the kind of project a buyer can understand fast — intimate, music-driven, and production-light — while still offering a lead performance that could matter to casting and awards-minded indie audiences.

items.area: The middle plays as montage more than drama.
items.detail: After Celia enters Pierre's life, the script leans heavily on quick flashes, voiceover, and lyrical transitions rather than scene-to-scene escalation. That keeps the tone consistent, but it also means the feature's central stretch has limited forward pressure for a buyer evaluating audience momentum.

items.area: The emotional beats are carrying the structure.
items.detail: The funeral speech and final voiceover do the heavy lifting, which makes the piece feel more like an elegy than a fully engineered feature narrative. Producers will notice that the script's impact depends on performance and mood more than on a strong sequence of reversals.

items.area: Novo Amor clearance is a real line item.
items.detail: The script specifically names 'Anchor' and 'Seneca,' so those tracks are not just temp references — they are clearance and budget items if the music stays in the cut. That is manageable, but it is a real cost and rights conversation for packaging.

items.area: The lead role narrows casting to a specific type.
items.detail: Pierre has to play awkwardness, poetic sensitivity, and grief without losing credibility as a teenager, which is a narrower ask than the page initially suggests. The role is attractive, but it will take a very particular young actor to make the inner life land cleanly.

issues.headline: The main friction is structural: the script is strongest as a mood piece, but the central stretch relies on montage and voiceover more than active dramatic turns. Add the named-music clearance and the need for a very specific teenage lead, and the project becomes a targeted indie buy rather than a broad commercial one.
